citation.description: Ticket description 'Root cause (reproduced deterministically on 2026-11-19)' and the comment's 'Reproduction (AC1)': a single-threaded scratch script gave byte_total 7 against an inode walk of 110 on every run. The same interleaving is encoded in test_evict_measures_then_a_populate_links_from_the_victim (tests/unit/test_snapshot_janitor.py:1036-1052).

criteria.criterion: The interleaving that produces the drift is reproduced deterministically and recorded on this ticket.

citation.description: Three interleaving tests each assert cache.byte_total(store) == _real_store_bytes(store). The fix is in src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py:198-218, where _evict holds accounting_lock from exclusive_size through the decrement. It is also in repo_snapshot.py:689-738, where _build_publish_account runs the donor build, publish and add_bytes_held under one lock hold.

criteria.criterion: The byte total matches the store walk under that interleaving, with a regression test.

citation.description: The three tests exist at tests/unit/test_snapshot_janitor.py:1036, 1055 and 1074. The ticket comment records the pre-fix run on origin/main 2ca3e28fcc6 as 'assert 51 == 311, 571 == 311, 51 == 311, 3 failed', repeated 3 times. It records the post-fix run as 60 passed, with each test reporting that the second actor 'waited on the accounting lock'. The _Other spy (lines 1000-1014) is installed only when accounting_lock exists, so the pre-fix failures are the byte-total assertion rather than a setup error.

criteria.criterion: The 3 interleaving tests fail on the pre-fix tree and pass with the fix (checked by running them on both trees; results recorded on this ticket).

citation.description: Ticket comment: change landed as Gerrit 3477, merged as 384e0af92d1. make verify ran on origin/main e7532d2b71c (which contains 3477): rc=0, 21543 passed / 31 skipped, integration tier 226 passed / 2 skipped, 2026-11-20 12:31-13:36 PST. This names a commit, an outcome and a timestamp. I could not re-run it with the read-only tools.

_evict, drain_trash and startup_sweep run under cache.accounting_lock. cache.py:98-127 adds accounting_lock and add_bytes_held, and cache.py:245 shows acquire no longer adds bytes itself. repo_snapshot.py:689-738 puts donor links, publish and exclusive_size accounting in one hold, and only the build whose rename published the entry adds bytes. The three deterministic interleaving tests cover the root cause and its two sibling interleavings.

criteria.criterion: Bug is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces and expected behavior holds.
